subject: POC closure playbook, exec readout slot & next-contract path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@novalytics.com>; Novalytics Procurement <procurement@novalytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-19 09:12:10 -0800
Subject: Recap & proposed POC plan (next steps + owners)

Hi Claire — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Summary of ask:
- Evaluate Redwood Inference for a 4-week POC focused on summarization accuracy and token-cost per conversation across your mid-size support dataset.
- Primary risks you called out: latency targets for sub-90 token responses, data retention controls for regulated records.

Proposed POC (high level):
1) 4-week evaluation window (pilot snapshot and steady-state week)
2) Success criteria (preliminary):
   • Latency: 95th percentile < 180 ms on 512-token context
   • Quality: ROUGE-L / human acceptability on a 200-item prompt set (target >= 0.78)
   • Cost: per-token unit cost below your current baseline by >= 12%
3) Owners:
   • Redwood SE: Jonas Weber (integration & metrics)
   • Redwood CS: Sean Gallagher (ops & monitoring)
   • Customer PM: Claire Zhang (success criteria sign-off)

Attachments & links:
- Attached: Redwood-POC-Plan-v1.pdf (outline + data checklist)
- Drive pre-read (will share updated eval matrix after your feedback)

Asks for this week:
- Claire: confirm acceptance of the high-level success criteria and confirm a preferred exec readout week (we recommend wk of Jan 4 or Jan 11) so we can reserve time for your stakeholders.
- Procurement: can you confirm typical SOW redline timeline so we can align the go/no-go decision to your onboarding windows?

I’ll follow up with a detailed eval matrix and propose owner-level milestones. Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0119

--
Attachment: Redwood-POC-Plan-v1.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

From: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@novalytics.com>

Cc: Novalytics Procurement <procurement@novalytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-20 11:04:33 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed POC plan (next steps + owners)

Thanks Marissa — that looks good overall. A couple quick clarifications before we lock timelines:

1) Latency: the 180 ms 95th pctl target is aggressive but acceptable for the pilot if it’s measured from our EU edge (we’ll want region-specific numbers in the readout).
2) Data retention: we need confirmation that KV/prefix cache clear can be enforced per-customer and that logs can be retained for 30 days only. Can you have a short note on that in the eval matrix?

Preferred exec readout: Jan 10 (any time after 1:00 PM PT) — that works best for our product and security stakeholders.

Procurement note: we typically take 10–14 business days to review minor SOW redlines; if vendor legal needs more time, flag it.

I’ll get procurement on-board on distribution and share their contact for redlines.

Claire
Claire Zhang
Director of Product, Novalytics
claire.zhang@novalytics.com

Claire — attached the eval matrix you asked for and a slightly expanded success criteria set. Highlights below and owners for each checkpoint.

Evaluation plan (deliverables & owners):
- Week 0 (kickoff): data ingest and baseline run (Jonas)
- Week 1–2 (sprint): integration + monitoring set up; run 500 sample prompts (Jonas + Novalytics eng)
- Week 3 (steady-state): run 2,000 convs to measure cost/latency (Sean monitors infra metrics)
- Week 4 (readout): produce executive-level dashboard + quality report (Marissa leads readout)

Success criteria (finalized):
- Latency: 95th pctl < 180 ms (measured from Novalytics US edge), regional callouts for EU if latency differs > 40 ms
- Quality: human acceptability >= 0.78 on agreed 200-prompt set (sampling & blind review)
- Cost: 12% unit-cost improvement vs current provider on average token-length profile
- Security: KV cache clearable per-customer; logs retention configurable to 30 days (ops proof required)

Attachments:
- novalytics-eval-matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB) — integration checklist + metric thresholds

HubSpot & pre-reads:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567
- Drive folder (eval docs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC

Next actions (this week):
- Claire: sign-off on the success criteria (reply ok/not ok)
- Novalytics eng: share initial sample dataset (s3 link) by EOD Friday
- Redwood: we’ll prep a short pre-read for the Jan 10 exec meeting (minutes + dashboard sample)

If that all looks good I’ll lock Jan 10 at 1:30 PM PT for the exec window and send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Jan 10 exec readout agenda + go/no-go gating & next contract step

Perfect — Jan 10 at 1:30 PM PT is on the calendar. Agenda and gating below so execs know what to expect.

Agenda (30 min + 15 Q&A):
- 5 min: Business summary & use case impact (Marissa)
- 10 min: Technical validation (Jonas) — latency, cost, and cache behavior evidence
- 10 min: Ops & adoption plan (Sean) — rollout and support model + SLOs
- 5 min: Decision & next steps (Marissa + Claire)

Go/no-go gating (requires majority of customer exec panel to say YES):
- All tech checks green: 95th pctl latency within 180 ms (US), cache flush proof demonstrated
- Quality gate: human acceptability >= 0.78 on the agreed sample set
- Contract path: procurement acknowledges SOW redline cadence and has shared primary contact

If the panel votes GO:
- Redwood to incorporate any minor redlines and issue final SOW for signature via DocuSign (link below). Target: SOW sent within 3 business days of readout.
If the panel votes NO or needs follow-up:
- Capture action items, schedule follow-up tech deep-dive (we’ll propose dates within 5 business days).

DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/link/to/SIGN-NOV-042

Thanks all — we’ll circulate the pre-read deck (one-page dashboard + eval highlights) by Jan 4 for your review.

-Marissa
